title: Literals: `INT`, then `BIGINT`, then `DECIMAL`; `1.5` is a decimal, `1e0` a double
verdict: `1` int; `2147483648` bigint; `1.5` decimal(2,1); `1e0`, `1.5D` double; suffixes `Y S L F D BD`
description: An integer literal is the narrowest of `INT`, `BIGINT` and `DECIMAL(p,0)` that holds it (`2147483648` is `bigint`, `9223372036854775808` `decimal(19,0)`). A literal with a point is a decimal (`1.5` is `decimal(2,1)`, `-0.0` `decimal(1,1)`), one with an exponent a `double` (`1e0`). Suffixes pick the type: `1Y` tinyint, `1S` smallint, `1L` bigint, `1.5F` float, `1.5D` double, `1BD` decimal. `NULL` is `void`; `array(1, 2L)` is `array<bigint>`.
So `2147483647 + 1` is `INT` arithmetic and raises under ANSI.
reference: Substrait literals carry their type; the frontends (the SQL lift, the Ibis producer) choose it, and the Spark writer casts each literal to its declared type.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_spark` runs each query four times on one local session: with `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` true and false, on the folded path (the optimizer evaluates a query over `VALUES` on the driver) and on the codegen path (`ConvertToLocalRelation` and `ConstantFolding` excluded, so the query runs as a job with whole-stage code generation). probes.json keeps one result per ANSI setting where the two paths agree. Spark 4.3.0 (pyspark 4.3.0), Java 21.0.12, Linux x86_64, `local[2]`, session time zone UTC, `spark.sql.timestampType=TIMESTAMP_NTZ`.
